sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **The Pact**: An informal agreement proposed by Bhulabhai Desai (Leader of Congress Party in Central Legislative Assembly) and Liaquat Ali Khan (Deputy Leader of Muslim League) in January 1945.
• **Core Proposal**: Formation of an interim government at the Centre consisting of equal number of persons nominated by Congress and League in the Central Legislature, 20% reserved for minorities, and the Commander-in-Chief as a member.
• **The Failure**: The Congress Working Committee (CWC) denied authorizing Desai, and Jinnah publicly disowned Liaquat Ali Khan, claiming he had no authority to negotiate.
• **Key Metric**: The pact was an attempt to break the political deadlock following the failure of the Gandhi-Jinnah talks (1944).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Official denial of authorization; Gandhi was skeptical of parity.
Internal party discipline and fear of conceding 'parity' to ML.
Prelims: Distinguish between individual initiative vs party policy.
Jinnah disowned the pact; insisted on 'Pakistan' as a precondition.
Jinnah's 'Two-Nation Theory' and refusal to accept parity without sovereignty.
Mains: Analyze why ML rejected parity in 1945 but demanded it later.

items.definition: The demand for equal representation of Hindus and Muslims in the executive, which became the central point of contention in all 1945 negotiations.
A transitional administration intended to manage the war effort and prepare for the transfer of power; the Desai-Liaquat pact was an attempt to form this without British mediation.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Legislative Maneuvering**: Desai attempted to use the Central Assembly as a platform for constitutional breakthrough.
• **Wavell's Role**: Lord Wavell was initially encouraged by the pact as it signaled a potential thaw in communal relations.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of transparency, absence of formal party mandates, and the 'Pakistan' demand.
• **Solutions**: The failure led to the formalization of the Wavell Plan (Simla Conference) to bring official parties to the table.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-L-D' (Desai-Liaquat-Denied).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Desai and Liaquat met, but both parties Denied the pact.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames questions suggesting the Desai-Liaquat pact was an official Congress-League agreement. It was strictly an 'informal' and 'unauthorized' effort.

Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Deadlock' to describe the 1944-45 period. The Desai-Liaquat pact is a classic example of 'Elite-level negotiation failure' in Indian constitutional history.

keyTakeaways: The Desai-Liaquat pact was an unauthorized, informal attempt to resolve the constitutional deadlock.
Both the Congress and the Muslim League leadership officially disowned the pact to maintain their respective bargaining positions.
The failure of this pact paved the way for the British-led Simla Conference (Wavell Plan) in June 1945.
